This interactive dashboard explores trends in **seismic activity near Mount Vesuvius** using data from the **2025-05-13 TidyTuesday** dataset.

The dataset records volcanic tremors from 2011 to 2025 and is used here to answer:

- <i class="bi bi-graph-up-arrow"></i> Has seismic activity changed in frequency or strength over time?
- <i class="bi bi-arrow-down-circle"></i> Are events occurring deeper underground?
- <i class="bi bi-activity"></i> How do depth and magnitude correlate?

---

## <i class="bi bi-grid-1x2"></i>Dashboard Features

The app allows dynamic filtering by:

- **Year Range**
- **Review Status** (`revised`, `preliminary`, or all)

It includes the following charts:

- <i class="bi bi-bar-chart"></i> *Seismic Event Timeline* — Count vs Average Magnitude over time
- <i class="bi bi-bullseye"></i> *Depth Scatterplot* — How deep earthquakes occur by year
- <i class="bi bi-grid-3x3"></i> *Heatmap by Depth Band* — Activity concentration across depth zones

## <i class="bi bi-lightbulb"></i>What I noticed

Has activity changed over time? Yes, and quite a lot. 2013 and 2014 were the quiet years. Things picked up from 2015, peaked between 2018 and 2020, eased off slightly for a few years, and then 2024 was the busiest year of all.

Are events getting deeper? Not really. Nearly everything happens in the top kilometre, and below 3 km the events are few and far between. The deeper ones are rare but recent though: the only events in the 9 to 10 km band were in 2024.
